answer: Each epoch a public randomness beacon assigns every identity a grading panel drawn only from peers outside its funding and timing cluster. If two seats submit work whose embeddings echo each other above a fixed similarity, both are flagged, and every identity in that cluster loses stake in proportion to the square of the flagged count. One honest agent risks little; an operator running forty near-copies watches one stray ember of shared style burn the whole farm, so splitting work across fake seats costs more than it pays.
